newsitem.title: BELGIUM: POLICE IN BELGIUM SEIZE CHILD PORN VIDEO TAPES.
newsitem.headline: POLICE IN BELGIUM SEIZE CHILD PORN VIDEO TAPES.

text.p: Belgian police have seized several sado-masochism, paedophile pornography video tapes, one of which shows a child who could be dead, the head of the country's Vice Squad told Reuters on Wednesday.
"We cannot tell if the child is drugged, asleep or dead. It is impossible. No murder is shown," Vice Squad chief Bernard Van Jansbergt said.
He said the child in question is shown at the very end of one of the tapes strapped motionless to a chair.
Van Jansbergt said that at least five different European children were in the films and at least two adults.
"There are sexual acts. Sodomy and fellatio," he said.

"It might eventually be possible to identify two or three of the children, all of whom, unusually, are of European appearance. The adults in the films never show their faces...but there are at least two people."
All the tapes were seized in two raids in November and earlier this month at the same address in the town of Verviers, eastern Belgium. Four people are currently under arrest.
Van Jansbergt stressed that there was no connection between the tapes, seized in November and January, and the case of child abduction, abuse and murder involving convicted rapist Marc Dutroux.
Dutroux was arrested in mid-August. Two days later two young, sexually abused girls were rescued from a secret dungeon in the cellar of a house he owns in the central Belgian city of Charleroi.
Over the next two weeks Dutroux led police to the bodies of four other dead girls and that of one of his former accomplices, Frenchman Bernard Weinstein.
The girls, two of whom starved to death, had gone missing more than a year earlier.

Van Jansbergt said there was also no link between the seven child porn video tapes and the seizure two weeks ago of some 1,000 tapes, CD-ROMs and video cameras in raids on more than 60 addresses across Belgium.
These raids had been based on information provided by authorities in France and Britain. Two people have been arrested.

"I was in charge of that file too and I can tell you it is completely separate," Van Jansbergt said, refusing to say how police came across the Verviers address other than "through our own investigations."
